TIGER/Line Shapefiles 2025, county subdivisions, North Dakota (tl_2025_38_cousub.zip)
sources.about: Cities, townships and unorganized territories as the Bureau had them on January 1, 2025; also the county areas the precinct parts are checked against.

notes.lines: Every line is the Secretary of State's, generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre). A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it.
notes.parts: The smallest area the Secretary of State publishes is a precinct part: a precinct cut wherever a city, ward, school, park or other district line crosses it. Each shape here is one part, named by its precinct's number and its own, and what is said of it (county, legislative district, city, ward, commissioner district, soil conservation district, judicial district, park district) is the Secretary's table's own word for that part.
notes.places: A part outside the cities is often several townships together, so the part does not say which township a voter lives in: the mcd layer (the Census Bureau's cities, townships and unorganized territories of January 1, 2025) answers that for a point. A part the Secretary's table puts in a city is given that city, whatever the Bureau's older city limits say.
notes.commissioners: The Secretary's table says how each county elects its commissioners: at large; one for each district by the voters of the whole county (the table lists every district on every part); or each by the voters of its own district. Only districts of the last kind are voting areas, so only they are shapes; supervisor_plans gives every county's.
notes.legislative: A legislative district elects one senator and two representatives; district 4 elects one representative from each of its subdistricts, 4A and 4B, told apart here by laying the Legislative Council's lines over the precinct parts (analysis).
notes.school: School district lines are the Department of Public Instruction's. Which districts a part lies in is analysis, not an official list: a district counts when its piece of the part is at least 60 metres thick somewhere; school_pct is each district's share of the part's area (land and water, not voters). The Secretary's table names a school district only on some parts (school_said). No school office is on the November 2026 ballot.
notes.wards: The Secretary's table names city wards for a few cities. Where it lists several wards on one part (the part is not cut along the ward lines), each of those wards is drawn as the whole part and marked shared.
notes.authority: For which precinct an address votes in, and where, the county auditor and the North Dakota Secretary of State's "Where do I vote" page are the authority.
notes.precinct_ids: A part's id is its precinct's six digits (the county's number in the alphabet, the legislative district, the precinct) and the part's two (47292007). Five parts the table numbers 9999.01 are filed as part 99 of their precinct.

format.files: Every file is TopoJSON on one grid (transform above): arcs are delta-encoded lines; a shape's arcs name the lines of its rings, a negative number n meaning line ~n backwards; outer rings run counter-clockwise, holes clockwise.
format.county_files: precincts/<county>.json, object 'precincts': one shape per precinct part. arcMask[i] has bit k set when line i is an outline of arc_kinds[k]; arcSides[2i] and arcSides[2i+1] are the parts on the right and left of line i (-1: a part in another county's file, or one just across a hairline gap in the state's drawing; -2: outside North Dakota); names gives the names of the places the file's parts lie in.
format.boxes: boxes[county] holds four whole numbers a part, in the file's order: west, south, east, north in steps of box_step degrees from the transform's translate, rounded outwards. A point is tried against every part whose box (widened by half a step) holds it.

precinct_properties.name: the precinct's name (Precinct 472920, part 07): its number in the Secretary's table and the part's
precinct_properties.mcd: city, township or unorganized territory holding most of the part (the table's own city where it names one)
precinct_properties.mcd_all: list, when the part reaches more than one: every city and township it lies in, largest share first
precinct_properties.mcd_pct: list, with mcd_all: each place's share of the part's area, in percent
precinct_properties.city: the city the Secretary's table puts the part in
precinct_properties.ward: list: the city ward the precinct lies in (absent where the table names none)
precinct_properties.com: county commissioner district (only in a county whose commissioners are each elected by their own district's voters)
precinct_properties.house: House district (the legislative district; 4A or 4B in district 4)
precinct_properties.garrison: true where the part lies in the Garrison Diversion Conservancy District
precinct_properties.sw_water: true where the part lies in the Southwest Water Authority
precinct_properties.ems: the ambulance or fire district the table names
precinct_properties.vector: true where the part lies in a vector control district
precinct_properties.library: the library district the table names
precinct_properties.school_said: the school district the table names, in its words
precinct_properties.split: only where a second House subdistrict holds 3 percent or more of the part: each one's share in percent
precinct_properties.school: list: the school districts the part lies in, largest share first
precinct_properties.school_pct: list, when the part is in more than one: each district's share of its area, in percent
precinct_properties.school_out: percent of the part's area that lies in no school district (given from 3 percent up)
precinct_properties.school_edge: list: neighbouring districts that only brush the part along a line (try them too when placing a point)
precinct_properties.c: a point inside the part's largest piece, for a label: [longitude, latitude]

ids.every layer: a shape's properties j and d are the jurisdiction id and the district its races carry on the ballot pages
ids.mcd: ND-M- and the Census county subdivision code (ND-M-07200); properties.t says city, township or unorganized territory
ids.cd: 0; properties.race is the race for Congress
ids.judicial: the ballot database's id (ND-SC); d is the district's name
ids.swcd: the ballot database's id (ND-X-015-burleigh-county-soil-conservation-district); j is the same
ids.park: ND-P-, the county's three digits and the park district's name (ND-P-017-fargo)
ids.school: ND-S- and the Department's five-digit district number (ND-S-08001)
